newsitem.title: INDIA: India PFC gets "go-ahead" for Euro issue - agency.
newsitem.headline: India PFC gets "go-ahead" for Euro issue - agency.

text.p: India's Finance Ministry has "given a go-ahead" for a proposal from state-run Power Finance Corporation (PFC) to launch a $100-125 million Euro issue, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Sunday.
The corporation is now trying to finalise lead managers and work out details for the Euro issue, and would shortly move a formal proposal to the ministry, the news agency said.

PFC negotiated a $75 million syndicated loan anchored by Natwest Bank in January, and approached the government for permission to launch a Euro issue as it wanted long-term international finance for a 10- to 12-year period, it said.
The Finance Ministry had also allowed PFC to retain up to 2.75 billion rupees ($76.82 million) from an ongoing issue of tax-free bonds through private placement, PTI said.

The ministry had earlier allowed PFC to raise 2.0 billion rupees from the bond issue, and a positive response to the offer had enabled PFC to secure approval for it to retain an additional 750 million rupees, it said.
The corporation, which lends funds for power projects, expects a five-fold increase in loan disbursals to 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion) during India's Ninth Plan (1997-2002), PTI said.
